documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Syllabus Guidance
documents.summary: Requires every instructor to include a generative AI statement in the syllabus, leaves the degree of AI use to instructors, and supplies a sample statement.
documents.stance_why: The page says "All Marshall instructors are required to have a generative AI policy" and "Instructors have the academic freedom to decide what degree of generative AI use should be integrated", so no university rule is set and the decision is delegated; the sample is only a template.

units.why: The sentence says "All Marshall instructors are required to have a generative AI policy in their syllabi", a mandate on instructors to state AI expectations, which is P09 (syllabus statement required), binding instructors before the course.
units.anchor: All Marshall instructors are required to have a generative AI policy in their syllabi.

units.why: "This policy should promote ethical decision making around generative AI use in class and students' future career" ties the syllabus policy to career preparation and ethical use; P44 (professional skill) fits best since the career framing is the stated purpose, while the content is not a stance.
units.anchor: mirrors industry/discipline norms, needs, and standards
units.policy: The syllabus policy should promote ethical decision making around generative AI use in class and in students' future career, modeled by instructors and mirroring industry/discipline norms, needs, and standards.

units.why: "Instructors have the academic freedom to decide what degree of generative AI use should be integrated in courses" leaves the AI rule to each instructor, per activity or assignment, which is P04.
units.anchor: Instructors have the academic freedom to decide
units.policy: Instructors have the academic freedom to decide what degree of generative AI use should be integrated in courses, focusing on specific types of use within individual activities, assignments, and learning exercises.

units.why: "You are also free to write your own policy statement" says instructors may use the template or write their own; it concerns who sets the rule, so P04 rather than P09.
units.anchor: You are also free to write your own policy statement.

units.why: The sample text says "use generative AI in any way that would violate the Student Code of Conduct" is not allowed, tying AI misuse to the conduct code, so P36 (misuse handled as misconduct) fits.
units.anchor: use generative AI in any way that would violate the
units.policy: Students may not use generative AI in any way that would violate the Student Code of Conduct.

units.why: "You may be allowed to use Generative AI in some ways but are prohibited from using it in other ways" in the sample statement sets a mixed, activity-by-activity rule rather than one default, so P04.
units.anchor: You may be allowed to use Generative AI in some ways but are prohibited
units.policy: Students may be allowed to use generative AI in some ways but are prohibited from using it in other ways during individual assignments, activities, and other learning exercises.

units.why: "Some assignments prohibit AI use entirely" states a full ban on certain assignments; it is assignment-level, so P01 (ban on graded work) is the closest type, not P04 which covers who decides.
units.anchor: Some assignments prohibit AI use entirely.

units.why: "See individual assignment instructions for more details" sends students to assignment-level instructions for the rule, so it is a per-assignment rule (P04) communicated at course start.
units.anchor: See individual assignment instructions for more details.

units.why: AI use "should be considered just like any other personal communication or secondary source of information", i.e. treated like an outside source under existing rules (P45).
units.anchor: considered just like any other personal communication or secondary source of information
units.frag_start: Generative AI use in this course
units.policy: Generative AI use in this course should be considered just like any other personal communication or secondary source of information.

units.why: The same sentence says AI output needs to be "critiqued, cross-referenced with primary sources of information", which is a duty to verify output (P31).
units.anchor: critiqued, cross-referenced with primary sources of information
units.frag_start: Generative AI use in this course
units.policy: AI output needs to be critiqued and cross-referenced with primary sources of information.

units.why: The sentence also requires that AI use be "properly cited", a duty to cite AI use (P24); the how-to details are not given here so not P25.
units.anchor: and properly cited
units.frag_start: Generative AI use in this course
units.policy: Generative AI use needs to be properly cited.

units.why: "For information on citing AI, please see the Marshall Library's citation website" points students to citation guidance, supporting the citation duty (P24).
units.anchor: Marshall Library’s citation website
units.frag_start: For information on citing AI, please see

units.why: "If there is any ambiguity about generative AI use in the course, please discuss with the instructor" tells unsure students to ask first (P10).
units.anchor: please discuss with the instructor

units.why: "The instructor should provide specific guidance on if and how AI usage is prohibited or allowed by students for each assignment, assessment, and/or lesson" requires instructors to put expectations in assignment-level instructions (P09, with assignment-level setting as in P04; P09 chosen because it is about communicating).
units.anchor: should provide specific guidance on if and how AI usage is prohibited or allowed
units.policy: The instructor should provide specific guidance on if and how AI usage is prohibited or allowed by students for each assignment, assessment, and/or lesson.

units.why: "Departments and programs should provide instructors with sample assignments" is support for instructors on addressing AI use, so P63 (supporting faculty) fits.
units.anchor: Departments and programs should provide instructors with sample assignments
units.policy: Departments and programs should provide instructors with sample assignments to show how ethical AI use is addressed and disclosed at the assignment level.

units.why: "for more information and training related to Generative AI at Marshall University" points instructors to university training and information, a faculty-support statement (P63).
units.anchor: for more information and training related to Generative AI at Marshall University

documents.title: Responsible use of AI at Marshall University
documents.summary: University responsible-use page covering approved tools, data protection and student use; encourages responsible student AI use and sets no per-course rules.
documents.stance_why: "Marshall University encourages students to use AI tools responsibly to support learning" is the page's stance toward student use, with no ban or per-instructor delegation stated; conditions are integrity, data protection and verification.

units.why: "should use only approved technologies when storing, processing, or sharing Institutional Data" limits AI-powered tools to vetted ones for institutional data, which is P50 (prefer vetted tools).
units.anchor: should use only approved technologies when storing, processing, or sharing Institutional Data
units.frag_end: institutional information and ensure appropriate use.

units.why: "All technology solutions, including AI-powered tools and personal productivity applications, must follow the University's technology governance and review requirements" binds AI tools to review; P50 (vetted tools) chosen over P65 since it addresses users.
units.anchor: must follow the University’s technology governance and review requirements

units.why: The Technology Governance Process reviews "artificial intelligence tools" for "security, privacy, compliance, accessibility, and institutional risk before adoption", an institutional vendor/tool review (P65).
units.anchor: reviewed for security, privacy, compliance, accessibility, and institutional risk before adoption
units.frag_start: Marshall University’s Technology Governance Process helps

units.why: "Faculty and staff should follow established review processes when considering new technologies" directs employees to the review process before adopting AI tools (P65, since it is about tool review rather than data protection).
units.anchor: should follow established review processes when considering new technologies

units.why: "Artificial intelligence can support teaching, learning, research, student services, and administrative work" opens the guidance with a framing of AI's value and risks, an institution-wide preamble (P56).
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence can support teaching, learning, research, student services, and administrative work

units.why: The Center for Teaching & Learning "provides a comprehensive set of resources aimed at helping faculty understand and integrate artificial intelligence", which is support for faculty (P63).
units.anchor: provides a comprehensive set of resources aimed at helping faculty understand and integrate

units.why: "Marshall University encourages students to use AI tools responsibly to support learning, research, and academic success" is a default welcome of AI use, P02.
units.anchor: encourages students to use AI tools responsibly to support learning, research, and academic success
units.frag_start: Marshall University encourages students to use

units.why: The sentence lists "maintaining academic integrity" as part of effective use; no type covers a general integrity expectation without a defined rule, so it is UNCOVERED (P29 needs submitted work to be own work, not stated here).
units.anchor: Effective AI use includes maintaining academic integrity
units.policy: Effective AI use includes maintaining academic integrity.
units.uncovered_note: General expectation that students maintain academic integrity when using AI, with no specific rule.

units.why: "protecting personal and university data" lists data protection as part of effective student AI use (P50).
units.anchor: protecting personal and university data
units.policy: Effective AI use includes protecting personal and university data.

units.why: "verifying AI-generated content for accuracy" tells students to check AI output (P31).
units.anchor: verifying AI-generated content for accuracy
units.policy: Effective AI use includes verifying AI-generated content for accuracy.

units.why: "being transparent about AI assistance when appropriate" asks students to disclose AI help, conditioned by "when appropriate" (P24).
units.anchor: being transparent about AI assistance when appropriate
units.policy: Effective AI use includes being transparent about AI assistance when appropriate.

units.why: "applying critical thinking and human judgment throughout the learning process" keeps the student as thinker (P32).
units.anchor: applying critical thinking and human judgment throughout the learning process
units.policy: Effective AI use includes applying critical thinking and human judgment throughout the learning process.

units.why: "As AI tools become more common in education, it is important to use them responsibly and ethically" states the principle behind the guidance, a framework statement (P56).
units.anchor: it is important to use them responsibly and ethically
units.frag_start: As AI tools become more common

units.why: "Marshall University encourages the appropriate use of AI while maintaining academic integrity, proper attribution" ties encouragement to attribution; attribution is a disclosure duty (P24).
units.anchor: proper attribution, and original scholarship
units.frag_start: Marshall University encourages the appropriate use
units.policy: Marshall University encourages the appropriate use of AI while maintaining proper attribution.

units.why: "original scholarship" is kept as a condition of AI use, meaning the submitted work remains the student's own (P29).
units.anchor: maintaining academic integrity, proper attribution, and original scholarship
units.frag_start: Marshall University encourages the appropriate use
units.policy: Marshall University encourages the appropriate use of AI while maintaining original scholarship.

units.why: "Microsoft 365 Copilot operates within Marshall University's secure Microsoft 365 environment" names a university-provided licensed AI tool (P17).
units.anchor: Microsoft 365 Copilot operates within Marshall University’s secure Microsoft 365 environment

units.why: Copilot "applies existing safeguards such as encryption, access controls, Multi-Factor Authentication" describes data protection of the sanctioned tool (P50).
units.anchor: applies existing safeguards such as encryption, access controls, Multi-Factor Authentication
